subject.title: fix(sessions): use account names for direct display

question: Should configured channel account names be the shared gateway fallback for opaque direct-session identifiers when no explicit label, group display name, or meaningful origin label exists?
rationale: The supplied proof establishes the requested behavior, but choosing a generic account-name fallback changes how existing sessions are identified and searched across channel configurations; that precedence is a maintainer-owned product contract.

options.title: Accept the fallback precedence
options.body: Merge after current-head CI completes if maintainers agree that an opaque direct peer identifier should resolve to the configured channel account name.

options.title: Narrow the fallback
options.body: Keep account names only for explicitly supported channel/session-key shapes if maintainers want to avoid a shared cross-channel display policy.

options.title: Pause for a broader identity policy
options.body: Hold this PR if session labels should instead be resolved through a broader binding or agent identity hierarchy tracked by the related session-display work.

recommendation.title: Accept the fallback precedence
recommendation.body: Merge after current-head CI completes if maintainers agree that an opaque direct peer identifier should resolve to the configured channel account name.

likelyOwner.reason: The related merged session-display baseline makes them the strongest available routing candidate for precedence intent.
